en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Turning Away, 35.
The Training Rule on Expulsion.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, Bhaddā Kāpilānī had entered the rains retreat at Sāketa.
Being pressed by some business, she sent a messenger to the nun Thullanandā, saying:
"If the noble lady Thullanandā would grant me a dwelling place, I would come to Sāvatthī."
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said,
"Come, I will give it to you.
Then Bhaddā Kāpilānī went from Sāketa to Sāvatthī.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā gave her dwelling place to Bhaddā Kāpilānī.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was learned, an eloquent speaker, confident, and skilled in delivering a discourse on the Dhamma.
Bhaddā Kāpilānī, too, was learned, an eloquent speaker, confident, and skilled in delivering a discourse on the Dhamma; she was highly esteemed and held in high honor.
People, thinking,
“The noble lady Bhaddā Kāpilānī is learned, an eloquent speaker, confident, capable of delivering a Dhamma discourse,
and highly esteemed,” would first attend upon Bhaddā Kāpilānī and only afterwards attend upon the bhikkhunī Thullanandā.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, overcome by jealousy,

being angry and displeased because of the thought, “These [other] bhikkhunīs, it is said, are few in desires, contented, secluded, unattached, and live with much courtesy and compliance,” threw Bhaddā Kāpilānī out of her dwelling.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How indeed can the noble lady Thullanandā, having given her dwelling to the noble lady Bhaddā Kāpilānī, then, being angry and displeased, drive her out?
… [as before] … “Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā, having given her dwelling to Bhaddā Kāpilānī, then, being angry and displeased, drove her out?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having given her dwelling place to Bhaddā Kāpilānī, then, being angry and displeased, drive her out?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faithful…” [and so on].
And thus, monks, let the nuns recite this training rule:

“Whichever nun, having given a dwelling place to another nun, being angry and displeased, should herself eject her or cause her to be ejected, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Whichever nun... [as above]... “Whichever nun”: [as above].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
"Of a bhikkhunī" means: of another bhikkhunī. "Upassaya" (dwelling) means: [a place where] bhikkhunīs reside.
It is called "fastened with a door-panel.
"Having given" means having given it oneself.
"Angry and displeased" means dissatisfied,
with a struck mind, having become stubborn.
"Should expel" means...
If she takes her from the womb and drags her out through the doorway, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she takes her through the doorway and drags her outside, it is an offense of expiation.
If she causes her to pass through many doors by a single effort, it is an offense of expiation.
"Causes to be expelled" means that if she commands another [to do so], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Even if she has been commanded only once, if she causes [the person] to pass through many doors, there is an offense of expiation.

If, having given a dwelling to one who is fully ordained, she—being angry and displeased and perceiving her as fully ordained—expels her or causes her to be expelled, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If, having given a dwelling to one who is fully ordained, she—being angry and displeased and being in doubt as to whether she is fully ordained—expels her or causes her to be expelled, there is an offense of expiation.

If, having given a dwelling to one who is fully ordained, she—being angry and displeased and perceiving her as not fully ordained—expels her or causes her to be expelled, there is an offense of expiation.
If she ejects her belongings or causes them to be ejected, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she ejects [the dwelling] that is not secured by a door-bolt or causes it to be ejected, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she ejects her belongings or causes them to be ejected from that [dwelling], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one drags out, or causes to be dragged out, a person who is not fully ordained—whether from an enclosed space with doors or an unenclosed space—one commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one drags out, or causes to be dragged out, that person’s requisites, one commits an offense of wrong-doing.
If one perceives a person who is not fully ordained as being fully ordained, one commits an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is not fully ordained, but she is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is not fully ordained, but she perceives her as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense—
If she ejects one who is shameless, or causes her to be ejected;
if she ejects her requisites, or causes them to be ejected;
or if she ejects one who is insane, or causes her to be ejected.
If she ejects her requisites, or causes them to be ejected;
if she ejects one who causes quarrels, who causes strife, who causes disputes, who causes idle chatter, or who causes legal issues in the Saṅgha, or causes them to be ejected;
if she ejects her requisites, or causes them to be ejected—[these are offenses].
If one expels, or causes to be expelled, a female pupil or a female co-resident who does not conduct herself properly;
or if one expels, or causes to be expelled, her requisites;
[this applies to] one who is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the fifth training rule.
